newsitem.title: BRAZIL: Maturity of Brazil external debt creeps up in Q3.
newsitem.headline: Maturity of Brazil external debt creeps up in Q3.

text.p: The average maturity of Brazilian overseas issues crept up marginally in the third quarter of 1996, the Central Bank said in a statement.
The Central Bank said the average maturity of total overseas issues was 7.2 years against 7.0 years in the second quarter.
That compared with an average maturity of 4.1 years in the third quarter of 1995.
The average spread remained stable across the two quarters at 465 basis points over U.S. Treasuries, versus 462 bps in the first quarter and 517 bps in the last quarter of 1995.
The bank's statement said the average global cost of the 77 Brazilian issues in the third quarter, totalling $3.735 billion, was 11.28 percent a year.
There were no issues by the public sector and all the paper was placed by private financial and non-financial organizations, with the non-financial sector enjoying cost and maturity advantages.
The average maturity of third quarter issues by banks was 5.8 years and the spread 525 bps. The average maturity for issues by companies was 7.5 years with a spread of 443 bps.
